sentences.zh: 盎格鲁-撒克逊时期的英格兰经常为此抱怨连天，那是整个基督教世界税赋最重的国家。

sentences.en: And just when the Anglo-Saxons thought it couldn't get any worse, they got conquered by King Canute.
sentences.zh: 正当盎格鲁-撒克逊人以为情况不会再恶劣时，他们被克努特国王征服了。

sentences.en: And Canute imposed a tax rate that was effectively 100%.
sentences.zh: 而克努特强加的税率实际上高达100%。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, that was one very big change, Tom.
sentences.zh: 是啊，汤姆，这确实是个巨大的改变。

sentences.en: But another tax change is upon us.
sentences.zh: 但另一项税收变革正在向我们走来。

sentences.en: And this is the advent of making tax digital for income tax.
sentences.zh: 这就是针对所得税的“数字化税收”计划的推出。

sentences.en: And if you're at all concerned about it, this is where Lloyd's come in, because they're here to help make that change much simpler for you
sentences.zh: 如果你对此有任何担忧，劳埃德银行可以为你排忧解难，因为他们致力于让这一变革对你而言变得更加简单，

sentences.en: with a useful HMRC-recognized accounting tool that will help you stay in line with all the making tax digital requirements.
sentences.zh: 他们提供了一款经英国税务海关总署（HMRC）认可的实用会计工具，能帮你轻松满足所有“数字化税收”的要求。

sentences.en: And the brilliant thing about this is that it is free for Lloyd's Business Account customers.
sentences.zh: 最棒的是，该工具对劳埃德商业账户客户完全免费。

sentences.en: So when it is time to digitize your income tax, you can bank on Lloyd's.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你的所得税需要数字化时，你可以完全信赖劳埃德银行。

sentences.zh: 搜索“劳埃德商业账户”了解更多信息。

sentences.en: Hello, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: So that was the national anthem of Brazil, one of the great World Cup teaMs.
sentences.zh: 刚才那是巴西的国歌，巴西是世界杯赛场上伟大的球队之一。

sentences.en: And we haven't actually had any Brazilian history, I think, since the last World Cup.
sentences.zh: 我想，自上届世界杯以来，我们实际上就再没有涉及过任何巴西历史。

sentences.en: So it is great to have them back.
sentences.zh: 所以很高兴他们能重归我们的节目。

sentences.en: And Brazil, of course, more closely associated with the World Cup, perhaps than any other team.
sentences.zh: 当然，比起其他任何球队，巴西或许都与世界杯有着更深厚的渊源。

sentences.en: They've won it a record five times.
sentences.zh: 他们创纪录地五次夺得世界杯冠军。

sentences.en: And the team that won in 1970 in Mexico, the team with Pele and everybody, often seen as the greatest national side of all time.
sentences.zh: 1970年在墨西哥夺冠的那支拥有贝利等球星的队伍，通常被视为史上最伟大的国家队。

sentences.en: Even though, Dominic, I think World Cup history specialists generally agree that England would have won that tournament,
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，尽管世界杯历史专家们普遍认为，如果不是因为

sentences.en: had the CIA not poisoned Gordon Banks, the England worldkeeper.
sentences.zh: 中央情报局对英格兰门神戈登·班克斯下毒，英格兰本会赢得那届锦标赛的胜利。

sentences.en: I don't think they do.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们才不会这么认为。

sentences.en: I think they probably do.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们很可能会。

sentences.en: Anyway, that's by the by.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，这都是题外话。

sentences.en: We lost to Brazil, as you will recall, Tom, in the groups.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，正如你所记得的，我们在小组赛中输给了巴西。

sentences.en: Remember that game?
sentences.zh: 还记得那场比赛吗？

sentences.en: I don't, because I was only two at the time.
sentences.zh: 我不记得，因为我当时才两岁。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Anyway, enough about football.
sentences.zh: 言归正传，足球的话题就到这里。

sentences.en: Let's move on to more important things, such as Don Pedro II, the last emperor of Brazil.
sentences.zh: 让我们转向更重要的事情，比如巴西的末代皇帝佩德罗二世。

sentences.en: And I mentioned him because he's very much a friend of the show, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 我提到他是因为他可以说是本节目的老朋友了，对吧？

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: He ruled from 1831 to 1889.
sentences.zh: 他从1831年统治到1889年。

sentences.en: But that's a kind of peripheral detail.
sentences.zh: 但这其实算是一种边缘细节。

sentences.en: What matters about Don Pedro is that he has a sensational beard.
sentences.zh: 关于唐·佩德罗，最要紧的是他有一部极具震撼力的胡须。

sentences.en: He loves the library.
sentences.zh: 他热爱图书馆。

sentences.en: He loves music.
sentences.zh: 他热爱音乐。

sentences.en: He loves scientific kind of all kinds of stuff, particularly meteorite.
sentences.zh: 他热爱各种科学，尤其是陨石。

sentences.en: Yeah, because he's sending, he was always sending people off on mad expeditions to recapture meteorites from the depths of the jungle and things.
sentences.zh: 对，因为他总是派人去进行疯狂的远征，从丛林深处等地把陨石找回来。

sentences.en: And I think that's what you want from a Brazilian emperor.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是你对一个巴西皇帝的期望。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, we've got him back today.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们今天把他请回来了。

sentences.en: Oh, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So hi, everybody.
sentences.zh: 那么大家好。

sentences.en: Our first foray into Brazilian history since the last World Cup.
sentences.zh: 这是自上届世界杯以来我们首次涉足巴西历史。

sentences.en: Last time, as Tom says, we did Don Pedro II.
sentences.zh: 正如汤姆所说，上次我们讲的是佩德罗二世。

sentences.en: This time we're doing the anthem.
sentences.zh: 这次我们讲的是国歌。

sentences.en: And Don Pedro II is returning.
sentences.zh: 而且佩德罗二世又回来了。

sentences.en: That's great to hear.
sentences.zh: 听到这个消息太棒了。

sentences.en: So a cameo appearance.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个客串出场。

sentences.en: We've also got the first man to see the Southern Cross.
sentences.zh: 我们还请到了第一个看到南十字座的人。

sentences.en: Well, certainly the first European to see the Southern Cross, anyway.
sentences.zh: 嗯，至少可以说是第一个看到南十字座的欧洲人。

sentences.en: And the Southern Cross is a star, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 南十字座是一颗星，对吧？

sentences.en: A constellation.
sentences.zh: 是一个星座。

sentences.en: It's a constellation.
sentences.zh: 是个星座。

sentences.en: We have some great characters.
sentences.zh: 我们有一些很棒的人物。

sentences.en: We've got a Jewish, a half-Jewish, half-Creole pianist from New Orleans.
sentences.zh: 我们有一位来自新奥尔良的犹太混血（一半犹太、一半克里奥尔）钢琴家。

sentences.en: And we have the Brazilian captain of the 1982 World Cup, who, Tom, you will admire because he had the excellent name.
sentences.zh: 我们还有1982年世界杯的巴西队长，汤姆，你会很佩服他，因为他有一个极好的名字。

sentences.en: Yeah, top philosopher.
sentences.zh: 对，顶级哲学家。

sentences.en: Socrates, exactly.
sentences.zh: 苏格拉底，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We've gained one or two listeners since the 2022 World Cup.
sentences.zh: 自2022年世界杯以来，我们增加了一两位听众。

sentences.en: And since we haven't done any Brazilian history before, and since Brazil's history is actually
sentences.zh: 鉴于我们以前没有做过任何巴西历史，而且鉴于巴西的历史

sentences.en: largely unknown outside Brazil, we should do a little bit of a sort of a panorama, a tour d'horizon.
sentences.zh: 在葡萄牙语世界之外实际上鲜为人知，我们应该做一个全景式的概述和宏观介绍。

sentences.en: Brazil, of course, is one of the world's biggest countries.
sentences.zh: 当然，巴西是世界上最大的国家之一。

sentences.en: It's the fifth biggest in size and the seventh in population.
sentences.zh: 它的面积居世界第五，人口居第七。

sentences.en: And it's presumably the country with the largest rainforeSt.
sentences.zh: 它大概也是拥有最大热带雨林的国家。

sentences.en: Yeah, undoubtedly.
sentences.zh: 是的，毫无疑问。

sentences.en: But its history, oddly, for such a vast country, is almost completely unknown outside the Portuguese speaking world.
sentences.zh: 但奇怪的是，对于这样一个幅员辽阔的国家，其历史在葡萄牙语世界之外几乎完全不为人知。

sentences.en: So to give you a sense of Brazil's story, until the 16th century, you've got this vast forested
sentences.zh: 为了让你对巴西的历史有个概念，直到16世纪，这里是一片广袤的森林

sentences.en: landscape, tropical landscape, where you have about 7 million indigenous people, semi-nomadic people, the Tupi, the Guarani, and so on.
sentences.zh: 热带景观，生活着大约700万原住民，即半游牧民族图皮人、瓜拉尼人等等。

sentences.en: And then in 1500, the first European fleet arrives under a Portuguese nobleman, Pedro Alvarez Cabral.
sentences.zh: 然后到了1500年，第一支欧洲舰队在葡萄牙贵族佩德罗·阿尔瓦雷斯·卡布拉尔的率领下抵达。
zh_words: 佩德罗·阿尔瓦雷斯·卡布拉尔

sentences.en: And Cabral called it the area that he found, he called it the Island of the True Cross, the
sentences.zh: 卡布拉尔将他发现的这个地区命名为“真十字架之岛”，即

sentences.en: Ilha de Veracruz.
sentences.zh: “圣克鲁斯岛”（Ilha de Veracruz）。

sentences.en: Once they discovered it wasn't an island, they called it the Terra de Santa Cruz, the land of the Holy Cross.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们发现这不是一座岛，便称之为“圣十字之地”（Terra de Santa Cruz）。

sentences.en: But within about a decade, so by the 1510s, people have started to call it the Terra do
sentences.zh: 但在大约十年内，也就是到16世纪10年代，人们开始称之为

sentences.en: Brazil.
sentences.zh: “巴西之地”（Terra do Brasil）。

sentences.en: And that's after the Brazil woods that they find there, which is a wood that gives you this red dye, this rich red dye.
sentences.zh: 这是因为他们在这里发现了巴西木，这是一种能提炼出浓郁红色染料的木材。

sentences.en: But if they hadn't had that rich red dye, they might have been called Vera Cruz.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们没有这种浓郁的红色染料，这里可能就被叫作韦拉克鲁斯了。

sentences.en: It would be.
sentences.zh: 确实会这样。

sentences.en: It would probably be called, or Santa Cruz, or something of that kind.
sentences.zh: 可能被称为圣十字或类似的名字。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: So under the Treaty of Tordesillas, which we talked about before when we were doing episodes about the conquistadors, the new world is divided between Portugal and Spain.
sentences.zh: 因此，根据我们在做征服者系列节目时谈到的《托德西利亚斯条约》，新世界在葡萄牙和西班牙之间进行了瓜分。

sentences.en: And because of miscalculations on the part of the Spanish, they don't realize how far into the Atlantic, basically, Brazil projects eastwards.
sentences.zh: 由于西班牙人的计算失误，他们没有意识到巴西向东延伸到大西洋的腹地有多深。

sentences.en: And Brazil falls under the jurisdiction of Portugal.
sentences.zh: 于是巴西落入了葡萄牙的管辖范围。

sentences.en: And this really is your classic example of what historians of imperialism called kind of extractive colonialism.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是帝国主义历史学家所称的“掠夺性殖民主义”的典型例子。

sentences.en: So they treat Brazil, the Portuguese, as a massive cash cow, and they are using it for its natural resources of sugar, gold, and coffee.
sentences.zh: 因此，葡萄牙人把巴西当作一台巨大的摇钱树，利用这里的自然资源生产糖、黄金和咖啡。

sentences.en: There's an issue, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 这里有个问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Because there aren't the kind of huge populations that are necessary to do this extraction.
sentences.zh: 因为根本没有足够庞大的人口来从事这种开采活动。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 完全没有。

sentences.en: A lot of the indigenous people, of course, die.
sentences.zh: 当然，许多原住民都死了。

sentences.en: They die of disease.
sentences.zh: 他们死于疾病。

sentences.en: Vast numbers of them die.
sentences.zh: 大量的人因此丧生。

sentences.en: And so the solution, as elsewhere in the new world, but on a much greater scale than anywhere else, is slavery.
sentences.zh: 因此，就像在新世界的其他地方一样，但规模远超其他任何地方，解决办法就是奴隶制。

sentences.en: This is the defining institution of Brazilian history, much more so than the United States, where we often think about slavery, we think about the United States, but Brazil looms
sentences.zh: 这是定义巴西历史的制度，远甚于美国——当我们想到奴隶制时，通常会想到美国，但巴西的奴隶制

sentences.en: a much larger.
sentences.zh: 其影响要巨大得多。

sentences.en: So almost half of the West African slaves transported across the Atlantic ended up on Brazilian plantations.
sentences.zh: 因此，被运送横越大西洋的西非奴隶中，将近有一半最终落在了巴西的种植园里。

sentences.en: So we're talking about four to five million people.
sentences.zh: 所以我们谈论的是四到五百万人。

sentences.en: And Brazil was actually the last country in the Western Hemisphere to abolish slavery in
sentences.zh: 事实上，巴西是西半球最后一个在
1888年废除奴隶制的国家。

sentences.en: And today, at least 60% of Brazilians, probably more, are descended from African slaves.
sentences.zh: 而今天，至少有60%的巴西人（可能更多）是非洲奴隶的后裔。

sentences.en: There's a brilliant history, basically the only real, really good English language history
sentences.zh: 有一部精彩的历史著作，基本上是唯一真正的、真正优秀的英文版巴西历史书，

sentences.en: of Brazil, by Lila Schwartz and Eloisa Starling, which I think I mentioned in the Dom Pedro second episode four years ago.
sentences.zh: 由莉拉·施瓦茨和埃洛伊萨·斯塔林合著，我想我在四年前的佩德罗二世节目中提到过它。

sentences.en: And in their book, they joke, I think it's quite a common joke in Brazil, that Brazil is the world's second largest African country after Nigeria.
sentences.zh: 他们在书中开玩笑说——我想这在巴西是个相当普遍的笑话——巴西是仅次于尼日利亚的世界第二大非洲国家。

sentences.en: And Dominic, can I ask you?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我可以问你吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 请说。

sentences.en: Imagine you're a slave being taken across the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 假设你是一个被带过大西洋的奴隶。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Would you rather go to the United States or Brazil?
sentences.zh: 你愿意去美国还是巴西？

sentences.en: Where would be worse?
sentences.zh: 去哪里会更糟糕？

sentences.en: I think no question, you'd rather go to the United States.
sentences.zh: 我想毫无疑问，你更愿意去美国。

sentences.en: Slavery in Brazil is hell on earth.
sentences.zh: 巴西的奴隶制简直是人间地狱。

sentences.en: It's awful.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: And what makes it so hellish?
sentences.zh: 是什么让它如此惨绝人寰？

sentences.en: It's extremely violent.
sentences.zh: 极其暴力。

sentences.en: There's no abolitionist movement in Brazil or a very small abolitionist movement compared with that in the United States.
sentences.zh: 巴西没有废奴运动，或者与美国相比，其废奴运动规模非常小。

sentences.en: It's much later.
sentences.zh: 而且要晚得多。

sentences.en: And is it also that the white exploitative class is much smaller relative to the number of slaves, so therefore they're more frightened?
sentences.zh: 是因为相对奴隶的数量而言，剥削人的白人阶层要小得多，所以他们更加恐慌吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: More insecure.
sentences.zh: 更加缺乏安全感。

sentences.en: So even by the standards of the new world, slavery in Brazil is extraordinarily cruel.
sentences.zh: 因此，即使按新世界的标准来看，巴西的奴隶制也残酷得无以复加。

sentences.en: And actually, it's a great question, where would you rather go?
sentences.zh: 实际上，这是一个很好的问题：你愿意去哪里？

sentences.en: And there's a very simple answer.
sentences.zh: 答案非常简单。

sentences.en: Most people, the single thing you want to do as a human being is to prolong your own life.
sentences.zh: 对绝大多数人来说，作为一个人类，你想做的一件最主要的事就是延长自己的寿命。

sentences.en: And in the United States, as a slave, you die at the age of 35.
sentences.zh: 在美国，作为一个奴隶，你到35岁就会死去。

sentences.en: As a slave in Brazil, you die at the age of 25.
sentences.zh: 而在巴西做奴隶，你到25岁就会死掉。

sentences.en: So there's your answer.
sentences.zh: 这就是答案。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And slave revolts, because it's very violent, because central authority is so weak, because cloning institutions are so fragile, slave revolts are much more common in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 由于它非常暴力，由于中央权威如此薄弱，由于各种建制如此脆弱，奴隶起义在巴西要常见得多。

sentences.en: So you have gigantic slave uprisings in the 18th and 19th centuries, which then provoke violent repression in their turn.
sentences.zh: 因此，你在18和19世纪会看到大规模的奴隶起义，而这反过来又会引发残酷的镇压。

sentences.en: So in their book on Brazilian history, Schwartz and Stalin describe the Brazilian plantations
sentences.zh: 因此，施瓦茨和斯塔林在他们的巴西历史著作中，将巴西的种植园描述为：

sentences.en: as, quote, hell on earth, a frenzy of cruelty, a world of violence rooted in the figure of
sentences.zh: 引述，“人间地狱，残忍的狂热，一个植根于主人及其法律赋予的至高无上权力的暴力世界，

sentences.en: the master and his supreme power under the law, the marks of which were constantly registered on the bodies of his slaves.
sentences.zh: 这种权力的烙印不断地刻在奴隶的躯体上。”

sentences.en: Now, why do I say all this when we're talking about the national anthem?
sentences.zh: 好了，当我们讨论国歌时，为什么我要说这一切？

sentences.en: Because the national anthem never mentions slavery at all, obviously.
sentences.zh: 因为国歌显然根本没有提到奴隶制。

sentences.en: It's not the kind of thing you would sing about, is it?
sentences.zh: 这不是那种你会用来歌唱的内容，对吧？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The answer is that, as we've discussed in previous episodes, Germany, the United States, the Dutch Republic, and so on, a national anthem tells a story about a country and about
sentences.zh: 答案是，正如我们在前几期节目中所讨论的，德国、美国、荷兰共和国等等，国歌讲述了一个关于国家的故事，讲述了

sentences.en: the sort of the idea of the nation as a united family.
sentences.zh: 将国家视为一个团结的大家庭的这种理念。

sentences.en: It's very difficult to do that in Brazil, because there's a fundamental instability that runs right through Brazilian history.
sentences.zh: 在巴西很难做到这一点，因为贯穿巴西历史的是一种根本性的动荡。

sentences.en: Weak central authority, the legitimacy of authority always being questioned, a constant tension
sentences.zh: 中央权威疲软，权威的合法性屡受质疑，

sentences.en: between the capital and the provinces, a sense that the next colossal rebellion is just around the corner.
sentences.zh: 首都与各省之间存在着持续的紧张关系，人们总觉得下一场惊天动体的叛乱就在拐角处。

sentences.en: It's hard to tell a collective story about Brazil's history, behind which everybody can unite.
sentences.zh: 很难讲述一个关于巴西历史的、能让所有人团结在背后的集体故事。

sentences.en: And that explains why, for so long, the national anthem didn't have any lyrics.
sentences.zh: 这就解释了为什么在很长一段时间里，国歌没有任何歌词。

sentences.en: Now, it wasn't a deliberate choice.
sentences.zh: 这并非刻意选择。

sentences.en: It was because they couldn't actually agree on what story they were going to tell.
sentences.zh: 而是因为他们实际上无法就该讲什么故事达成一致。

sentences.en: I mean, I suppose if we think about so many of the anthems that we've done, done, the idea of kind of liberty and freedom is, I mean, a fairly common theme.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果我们回想一下我们做过的那么多国歌，关于那种自由解放的理念，我的意思是，是一个相当普遍的主题。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And obviously, that's impossible, isn't it, in the context of Brazil?
sentences.zh: 显然，在巴西的语境下，这是不可能的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，确实如此。

sentences.en: Well, you need an enemy, often, with an anthem.
sentences.zh: 嗯，通常你需要一个带有国歌的敌人。

sentences.en: So, for the Americans, it was the British.
sentences.zh: 所以，对美国人来说，敌人是英国人。

sentences.en: For the Dutch, it was the Spanish, you know, even though their anthem is quite ambiguous about their relationship with the Spanish.
sentences.zh: 对荷兰人来说，是西班牙人，你知道的，尽管他们的国歌对他们与西班牙的关系表达得相当含糊。

sentences.en: The Germans, it was actually the French.
sentences.zh: 德国人，其实是法国人。

sentences.en: And for the British, it's the Spanish and the French.
sentences.zh: 而对英国人来说，则是西班牙人和法国人。

sentences.en: There's almost always an adversary.
sentences.zh: 几乎总会有一个对手。

sentences.en: And in Brazil, as we'll come to, it is, at first, the Portuguese.
sentences.zh: 而在巴西，正如我们接下来要谈到的，一开始是葡萄牙人。

sentences.en: So, let's get to the story of why Brazil needs an anthem in the first place.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们来聊聊为什么巴西一开始会需要一首国歌。

sentences.en: So, we start at the beginning of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们从19世纪初开始讲起。

sentences.en: So, in 1808, the government general of Brazil, as it's called, is the biggest state in Portugal's colonial empire.
sentences.zh: 在1808年，被称为巴西总督辖区的地方是葡萄牙殖民帝国中最大的州。

sentences.en: It's got about two and a half million people.
sentences.zh: 那里大约有两百五十万人口。

sentences.en: So, it's slightly smaller than Portugal itself.
sentences.zh: 所以，它比葡萄牙本土略小一点。

sentences.en: And a third of those people are slaves.
sentences.zh: 其中三分之一的人口是奴隶。

sentences.en: There are two big cities, Rio and Salvador.
sentences.zh: 有两个大城市，里约热内卢和萨尔瓦多。

sentences.en: And there, the slave population is actually bigger, probably half in Rio, three quarters in Salvador.
sentences.zh: 在那里，奴隶人口实际上更多，在里约可能占了一半，在萨尔瓦多则占了四分之三。

sentences.en: There's a sort of Wild West vibe to these places.
sentences.zh: 这些地方有一种类似美国西部荒野的风情。

sentences.en: So, people who visit, say, streets are pothole.
sentences.zh: 因此，来访的人说，街道到处都是坑洼。

sentences.en: They're full of rubbish.
sentences.zh: 到处都是垃圾。

sentences.en: It's all very chaotic and very violent.
sentences.zh: 整个地方非常混乱，而且极其暴力。

sentences.en: And one British visitor called Rio, one of the dirtiest congregations of human beings under the sun.
sentences.zh: 曾有一位英国访客将里约称作“阳光下最肮脏的人类聚集地之一”。

sentences.en: If you're a refined, elegant Portuguese courtier, Rio is basically the last place in the world that you would ever want to live.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个精致、优雅的葡萄牙朝臣，里约基本上是世界上你最不想居住的地方。

sentences.en: However, you are going to have to live there.
sentences.zh: 然而，你又不得不住在那里。

sentences.en: Because in the summer of 1807, Napoleon Bonaparte had lost patience with Portugal's refusal to join his continental system.
sentences.zh: 因为在1807年夏天，拿破仑·波拿巴对葡萄牙拒绝加入其大陆体系失去了耐心。

sentences.en: So, this is the blockade, the embargo against Britain to try and drive Britain out of the
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一场封锁，是对英国的禁运，试图将英国挤出

sentences.en: Napoleonic Wars.
sentences.zh: 拿破仑战争。

sentences.en: And the French and the Spanish, in November 1807, invaded Portugal, and they basically stormed towards Lisbon.
sentences.zh: 1807年11月，法军和西班牙军队入侵了葡萄牙，他们几乎是直扑里斯本。

sentences.en: By the time they got to Lisbon, they found that the entire Portuguese royal family, the whole of the court, most of the political elite, had gone.
sentences.zh: 当他们到达里斯本时，发现整个葡萄牙王室、所有的朝臣以及大部分政治精英都已经离开了。

sentences.en: They had embarked on British ships under Sir Sidney Smith, which were about almost 15,000 people, and they had sailed off to Brazil.
sentences.zh: 他们在西德尼·史密斯爵士的率领下登上了英国船只，那是将近15,000人，然后他们扬帆驶向了巴西。

sentences.en: An absolutely unprecedented moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个绝对史无前例的时刻。

sentences.en: You know, the entire court fleeing across the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，整个朝廷横渡大西洋逃亡。

sentences.en: So, it's a bit like the plans that were made to remove the British royal family in 1940.
sentences.zh: 所以，这有点像1940年制定计划撤离英国王室的那种情况。

sentences.en: To Canada.
sentences.zh: 去加拿大。

sentences.en: To Canada.
sentences.zh: 去加拿大。

sentences.en: In the US, exactly.
sentences.zh: 在美国，确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And chief among them are the Queen of Portugal, Dona Maria, who is kind of out of public life.
sentences.zh: 其中最核心的是葡萄牙女王多娜·玛丽亚，她基本上已经淡出了公众视线。

sentences.en: She's got massive depression and mental illness.
sentences.zh: 她患有严重的抑郁症和精神疾病。

sentences.en: And her son and regent, who is João, and his son, Pedro.
sentences.zh: 还有她的儿子兼摄政王若昂，以及若昂的儿子佩德罗。

sentences.en: So, three generations.
sentences.zh: 所以是三代人。

sentences.en: And off they all go, and they establish their court in Rio.
sentences.zh: 然后他们全体出发，在里约建立了自己的朝廷。

sentences.en: And here, they run their empire in exile.
sentences.zh: 在这里，他们在流亡中统治着他们的帝国。

sentences.en: So, this is the first time in history that an empire has been governed, not from the metropolis, but from a colony that is in both the Western and the Southern hemisphere.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是历史上第一次，一个帝国不是由本土统治，而是由一个同时位于西半球和南半球的殖民地来统治。

sentences.en: So, it's a sort of really interesting kind of transfer of power from Europe to the Americas.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种非常有趣的权力从欧洲向美洲的转移。

sentences.en: Anyway, 1815, Napoleon's beaten at Waterloo.
sentences.zh: 总之，1815年，拿破仑在滑铁卢战败。

sentences.en: And a year later, Dona Maria, who is the sort of nominal queen of Portugal, dies.
sentences.zh: 一年后，作为葡萄牙名义上的女王的多娜·玛丽亚去世了。

sentences.en: So, now her son, João, is Dom João VI, king of Portugal.
sentences.zh: 所以，现在她的儿子若昂成为了若昂六世国王，葡萄牙国王。

sentences.en: But he's still in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 但他仍然在巴西。

sentences.en: And he's still in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 而且他依然在巴西。

sentences.en: He's still in Rio.
sentences.zh: 他还在里约。

sentences.en: So, Dom João is a very shy man.
sentences.zh: 所以，若昂国王是一个非常害羞的人。

sentences.en: He's very religious.
sentences.zh: 他非常虔诚。

sentences.en: He basically spends all his time listening to sacred music.
sentences.zh: 他基本上把所有时间都用来听宗教音乐。

sentences.en: So, listening to antheMs.
sentences.zh: 也就是听圣歌。

sentences.en: Yeah, he listens to anthems, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，他听圣歌，确实如此。

sentences.en: He's got constant panic attacks.
sentences.zh: 他经常恐慌发作。

sentences.en: He's always depressed.
sentences.zh: 他总是很沮丧。

sentences.en: He wears the same coat all the time, even in bed.
sentences.zh: 他随时随地都穿着同一件大衣，甚至睡觉时也穿着。

sentences.en: He loves this coat.
sentences.zh: 他太爱这件大衣了。

sentences.en: I mean, I've got to say, he does not sign the Count of Man.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我得说，他可没签什么曼恩伯爵。

sentences.en: He could have taken on Napoleon.
sentences.zh: 他本可以对抗拿破仑的。

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: He's done well getting out to Rio.
sentences.zh: 他能逃到里约已经干得不错了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And he is in no hurry to go back to Portugal.
sentences.zh: 而且他一点也不急着回葡萄牙。

sentences.en: If he went back to Lisbon, the nobility, the political elite, political reformers, liberal constitutionalists would just be badgering him the whole time.
sentences.zh: 如果他回了里斯本，贵族、政治精英、政治改革派、自由立宪主义者整天都会缠着他。

sentences.en: But what about all the potholes in Rio and the rubbish?
sentences.zh: 但是里约那些坑坑洼洼的道路和垃圾怎么办呢？

sentences.en: He doesn't mind the potholes because Rio also has lovely birds and he's a big nature lover.
sentences.zh: 他不介意那些路坑，因为里约还有可爱的鸟类，而且他是个狂热的自然爱好者。

sentences.en: So, he goes on expeditions to the countryside to look at the nature, nice trees and plants, tropical shrubs.
sentences.zh: 所以他会去乡村探险，观察大自然、漂亮的树木和植物、热带灌木。

sentences.en: Is he a fan of volleyball?
sentences.zh: 他是排球迷吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I don't think they're doing volleyball at this point.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们那时候还不玩排球。

sentences.en: So, at the end of 1815, he elevates Brazil to the same level as Portugal.
sentences.zh: 所以在1815年底，他将巴西提升到与葡萄牙平等的地位。

sentences.en: So, he now rules a kingdom called the United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves.
sentences.zh: 因此，他现在统治着一个名为“葡萄牙、巴西和阿尔加维联合王国”的国家。

sentences.en: I don't know exactly why the Algarves are plural.
sentences.zh: 我不太清楚为什么阿尔加维是复数形式。

sentences.en: Maybe listeners can explain that to me.
sentences.zh: 也许听众可以向我解释一下。

sentences.en: Now, back in Portugal, the sort of liberal elites in Porto and Lisbon understandably hate this.
sentences.zh: 现在，回到葡萄牙，波尔图和里斯本的那些自由派精英们理所当然地痛恨这一点。

sentences.en: They're like, why on earth have we ceded first place?
sentences.zh: 他们觉得，凭什么我们要把第一的位置让出去？

sentences.en: Why are we sharing it with these upstarts in Brazil?
sentences.zh: 凭什么我们要和巴西这些暴发户平起平坐？

sentences.en: Also, Portugal's in a massive mess after the Napoleonic Wars.
sentences.zh: 此外，拿破仑战争之后的葡萄牙陷入了一团糟。

sentences.en: Their harvests have failed.
sentences.zh: 他们的农作物歉收。

sentences.en: Their economy's in ruins.
sentences.zh: 他们的经济一片废墟。

sentences.en: They're no longer really top dog in their own empire.
sentences.zh: 他们在自己的帝国里已经不再是真正的大佬了。

sentences.en: They're very cross.
sentences.zh: 他们非常生气。

sentences.en: And then, spring of 1821, they sent Dom João an ultimatum and they said, come back to Portugal or else, basically.
sentences.zh: 然后，在1821年春天，他们向若昂国王发出最后通牒，基本上是说，要么回葡萄牙，要么走着瞧。

sentences.en: And he said, oh, fine, very disconsolately.
sentences.zh: 他很不情愿地叹了口气说，好吧，好吧。

sentences.en: And before he left, he called in his 22-year-old son, Pedro.
sentences.zh: 在他离开之前，他把22岁的儿子佩德罗叫了进来。

sentences.en: So, this is the future Dom Pedro I.
sentences.zh: 也就是未来的佩德罗一世。

sentences.en: And he says to Pedro, I'd like you to stay in Rio.
sentences.zh: 他对佩德罗说，我希望你留在里约。

sentences.en: You're going to be my regent in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 你将成为我在巴西的摄政王。

sentences.en: Now, he and Pedro don't get on at all, but this is the only time they ever have any connection.
sentences.zh: 现在，他和佩德罗关系一点也不好，但这却是他们之间唯一的紧密联系。

sentences.en: Because João says to Pedro, Pedro, if Brazil breaks away, it would be better that it is by your hand than by the hand of some adventurer.
sentences.zh: 因为若昂对佩德罗说，佩德罗，如果巴西要分裂，由你亲手来做，也总比让某个冒险家来做要好。

sentences.en: Oh, essentially, the king of Portugal and Brazil is basically telling his own son to lead a secessionist movement.
sentences.zh: 哦，基本上，葡萄牙和巴西的国王居然在指使自己的儿子领导分裂运动。

sentences.en: Kind of, yeah.
sentences.zh: 算是吧，对。

sentences.en: That's unexpected.
sentences.zh: 这挺出乎意料的。

sentences.en: You could say he's being farsighted.
sentences.zh: 你可以说他很有远见。

sentences.en: That's another first for Portugal.
sentences.zh: 这又是葡萄牙的又一个第一。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's being farsighted.
sentences.zh: 是的，他很有远见。

sentences.en: He's basically saying, probably Brazil is going to try and break away.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是在说，巴西可能迟早会试图分裂。

sentences.en: I would like it to stay in the family.
sentences.zh: 我希望肥水不流外人田。

sentences.en: If it looks like it's going to break away, you'd be on the right side.
sentences.zh: 如果看来它注定要分裂，你站在正确的一边就行。

sentences.en: So, it would be a bit like the Prince Regent being the governor of New York or something and leading the revolution.
sentences.zh: 所以，这有点像摄政王担任纽约州长之类的人，然后领导了革命。

sentences.en: George III being summoned back by angry mercantile elites in London and saying to the Prince Regent before he leaves,
sentences.zh: 就像乔治三世被伦敦愤怒的商业精英召回，并在离开前对摄政王说，

sentences.en: if the colonists refuse to pay their taxes, put yourself on their side and then it'll stay in the family.
sentences.zh: 如果殖民地拒绝纳税，你就站到他们那边去，这样江山还是在自己手里。

sentences.en: So, an alternative history in which the first leader of the United States is the Prince Regent.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个美国的第一任领导人是摄政王的架空历史。

sentences.en: What could have been?
sentences.zh: 那会是怎样呢？

sentences.en: I mean, he's got his own teeth, which is something you could say for him.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他有自己的真牙，这也是你可以夸他的一点。

sentences.en: Yes, that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，这倒也是。

sentences.en: So, now we have the very strange situation where Joao has gone back to Lisbon, but Pedro is the top dog in Rio.
sentences.zh: 所以，现在出现了一个非常奇妙的局面：若昂回到了里斯本，而佩德罗成了里约的老大。

sentences.en: And Pedro is an interesting character.
sentences.zh: 而且佩德罗是一个很有趣的人物。

sentences.en: He's very intelligent.
sentences.zh: 他非常聪明。

sentences.en: He's very well-read.
sentences.zh: 他博览群书。

sentences.en: He loves all the new liberal ideas.
sentences.zh: 他热爱所有的新自由主义思想。

sentences.en: He's been reading Voltaire.
sentences.zh: 他读过伏尔泰。

sentences.en: He's been reading Edmund Burke.
sentences.zh: 他读过埃德蒙·伯克。

sentences.en: He's also, you know, as is so often the way, spoiled, impulsive, erratic.
sentences.zh: 当然，就像很多这类人一样，他也有些被宠坏、冲动、喜怒无常。

sentences.en: But he's not hiding out in bed wearing a coat.
sentences.zh: 但他可没有躲在床上穿着大衣。

sentences.en: No, he's not wearing his coat in bed.
sentences.zh: 对，他可没有穿着大衣睡觉。

sentences.en: He's more proactive.
sentences.zh: 他更有进取心。

sentences.en: He's a bit of a lecher, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实他还有点好色。

sentences.en: He's a hit with the ladies.
sentences.zh: 他在女人中很吃得开。

sentences.en: So, his coat would not come in handy.
sentences.zh: 所以他的大衣在这种时候可派不上用场。

sentences.en: Because he's grown up and spent so much of his life in Rio, he cares much more about Brazil than he does about Portugal.
sentences.zh: 因为他在里约长大并度过了大半生，他比葡萄牙更关心巴西。

sentences.en: And the local politicians recognize this and they say, well, if we work on this guy, we can use him as a figurehead to get independence.
sentences.zh: 当地的政客们意识到了这一点，他们说，如果我们拉拢这家伙，我们就可以利用他作为争取独立的傀儡。

sentences.en: Who wants to be pushed around by a load of people who make port and corks or whatever they're making back in Portugal?
sentences.zh: 谁想被一群在葡萄牙本土酿造波特酒、做软木塞或者生产其他什么东西的人呼来喝去？

sentences.en: Who cares about them?
sentences.zh: 谁在乎他们啊？

sentences.en: We can pursue our own destiny.
sentences.zh: 我们可以追求我们自己的命运。

sentences.en: In December 1821, the Portuguese, who have kind of got wind of all this, they asked Pedro to come back to Lisbon as well.
sentences.zh: 1821年12月，风闻此事的葡萄牙人要求佩德罗也回到里斯本。

sentences.en: Because they thought, you know, him staying in Brazil is just encouraging separatism.
sentences.zh: 因为他们认为，他留在巴西只会助长分裂主义。

sentences.en: And then the Brazilians presented him with a petition signed by 8,000 people.
sentences.zh: 然后，巴西人向他呈递了一份有8000人签名的请愿书。

sentences.en: This is a very famous moment in Brazilian history, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这是巴西历史上非常著名的一个时刻，汤姆。

sentences.en: I'm sure you're over it.
sentences.zh: 我确信你对这个很熟。

sentences.en: This was a reception at the Royal Palace in Brazil in January 1822.
sentences.zh: 这是1822年1月在巴西王宫举行的一场招待会。

sentences.en: He gets given this petition.
sentences.zh: 他收到了这份请愿书。

sentences.en: He's very touched.
sentences.zh: 他深受触动。

sentences.en: And he says, as it is for the good of all and for the general happiness of the nation, I am ready.
sentences.zh: 他说，既然为了大众的利益和民族的普遍幸福，我已准备好了。

sentences.en: Tell the people I will stay.
sentences.zh: 告诉大家，我将留下来。

sentences.en: Hurrah, hurrah.
sentences.zh: 万岁，万岁。

sentences.en: Everyone in Rio is very pleased.
sentences.zh: 里约的每个人都非常高兴。

sentences.en: They can see what's coming.
sentences.zh: 他们预见到接下来会发生什么了。

sentences.en: So, eight months go by.
sentences.zh: 于是，八个月过去了。

sentences.en: And then on the 28th of August, 1522, a ship arrives in Rio from Lisbon.
